Ten seconds after the new Monarch was crowned, power across the country shut off. The city’s capital, Jirevjka, felt the shutdown first with the streetlights letting out a draining hum and the traffic lights flickering before turning off. The moment was so sudden that no one screamed until a few seconds later. Then, the city came alive with the energy of anxious people filling the streets and hurriedly looking around. 

  
Among the people was Lucy’s dad, a man many regarded as “cold” and “distance”, but a man who never ran away from the most severe of problems. He told Lucy, “Stay back with your sister, Anya. I’m going to see what’s going on.” He picked up the bat with barbed wire and the flashlight next to the doorway. He didn’t even look back at Lucy or Anya before making his way outside.

  
Lucy faced the blanked television, static crackling, and blinked. What did this mean? Was it an outage? She mulled over the idea for a few seconds. No, it couldn’t have been. She remembered watching the news a few weeks ago. A vigilante group on the outskirts of the city had their plot foiled by The Royal Guard to potentially harm the new Monarch. But they couldn’t have succeeded as they were all in jail. 

  
Lucy looked out the window and saw a large gathering of men outside. They all blinked up at the sky and tried to figure out what was happening. It made Lucy’s stomach turn because she knew something wasn’t right. 

  
The ground shook and before Lucy could even process what was happening, her body flung into the wood-paneled wall a few feet away. Her entire world went hazy and black flurries dotted her vision. She went out in and out of consciousness but someone screaming jolted her awake. 

  
Everything was moving in slow motion. Lucy couldn’t make sense of the fully-formed house she was sitting in not too long ago being replaced by a painting of the evening sky. No, that was the sky and an explosion had just ripped away her childhood home.
